When a title changes, `updateIssue` in [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/services/issue-service.ts) checks organization scope and `issue:update` permission, loads the existing issue, rejects an archived issue, and calls `issueRepo.updateIssue`. After the write, it awaits `emit("issue.updated", …)` with the issue ID and changed field names.

The listener is installed at server startup: `register` in [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/instrumentation.ts) calls `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/services/event-registry.ts), which calls `registerSearchListeners` in [search-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/services/search-service.ts). The `issue.updated` listener re-reads the saved issue by organization and ID, then calls `indexIssue`. That calls `upsertSearchDocument` in [search-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts), updating the existing document identified by organization, kind and subject ID, or inserting one.

`emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for all subscribers to settle, so a successful listener normally finishes before `updateIssue` returns. It isolates subscriber failures, though: a failed indexing handler does not fail the issue write. Thus synchronization is not guaranteed if a handler fails or is absent. The listeners also index issue and comment creation and project creation, remove documents on issue/project archival or comment deletion, and handle issue `search.reindex_requested` events. `runSearchReindexJob` in [search-reindex-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts) re-upserts content for an organization for recovery after imports or drift; its current implementation reads the first page of up to 100 projects, issues and comments per issue.

The searchable copy is the SQLite `searchIndex` table defined in [webhooks.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts). Each row stores an ID, organization ID, subject kind and ID, optional project ID, content, and indexing timestamp. `indexIssue` stores the title and description separated by a newline; `indexProject` stores name and description similarly; `indexComment` stores its body and no project ID. The table has an organization/kind index, but searching the content itself is a substring `LIKE` query.

On the read side, the full-page `Page` in [search/page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx) loads the tenant and actor, checks `advanced_search`, and validates the text with `searchQuerySchema` from [search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/schemas/search.ts). It requests issues alone without the flag, or issues, comments and projects with it. The schema requires 1–200 characters and validates kinds, optional project ID and pagination. The command-palette `GET` in [api/search/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/app/api/search/route.ts) also obtains an actor, checks organization read permission and the `command_palette` flag, validates the request, and calls the same service.

`search` in `search-service.ts` then checks tenant scope and `issue:read`, consumes the organization’s `search:query` rate-limit token, loads the organization and evaluates `advanced_search` with its plan, role and overrides. **A schema-valid query can still be refused** if authorization fails, the shared organization bucket is exhausted, or its text contains *any colon* while advanced search is disabled. That last rule includes a literal colon in an otherwise ordinary title; it returns “Field-scoped search is not included in this plan.” The bucket is configured in [rate-limit.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/lib/rate-limit.ts) with capacity 120 and refill of 60 per minute.

If those gates pass, `searchDocuments` filters by organization, content, requested kinds and optional project, counts matches, and returns a keyset-paginated page ordered by newest indexing timestamp and ID. `search` maps each row into a `SearchHit`: its first content line becomes the title, `snippetAround` extracts surrounding context, and `hrefFor` builds a subject link. The page renders those hits; the API returns items and total as JSON.

The separate `SearchDialog` in [search-dialog.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx) debounces input and calls `parseSearchQuery` in [query-syntax.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/734be434-f98a-4f7f-98a7-db3840f0c0c9/src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts) before invoking its supplied `onSearch`. With advanced search enabled, that parser extracts recognized `kind:`, `in:` and `project:` tokens into filters and sends the remaining text; unknown tokens are ignored. Without it, the parser leaves the trimmed text intact, so the service’s colon rejection still applies.
